g.text: How to choose a model: what to weigh, and why the only answer you can defend is the
one you measured on your own tasks.
lessons/12-choosing-a-model/run.py (the prompts live here; the exercises ask you to
The story below is the setting. LANTERN is the local model; the case files are the text you send it.
Varma has a rule about tools: you do not trust one you have not tested. LANTERN carries three models of
the same family, a small one, a medium one and a large one. Okafor wants the large one for everything.
The duty sergeant wants answers before the morning briefing. Hale wants to know, in writing, why you
chose the one you chose. You set up a fair test: the same sixteen messages from Reyes's phone, the same
invoice, the same settings, and a stopwatch.
The classification prompt is the `CLASSIFY` variable in run.py. `LABEL_SCHEMA` pins the answer to three
Same tasks, same settings, temperature 0, CPU only
latency/msg is Ollama's own timing per message, excluding model load and queueing.
Read the table as a trade: each row down buys accuracy with time and memory.
Your numbers will differ on a GPU. The method is the lesson, not the figures.
1. Read the scorecard row by row. Where does accuracy go up, and what does each step to a bigger model
cost in latency, memory and cold start?
2. Compare each model's 'extraction:' line with case/invoices/NW-0402.txt. Is every value in the field
3. Read the 'miss:' lines for all three models and look the ids up in case/messages.jsonl. Are the
misses spread across labels, or do they cluster?
1. Pull a fourth model (ollama pull llama3.2:3b) and add "llama3.2:3b" to `MODELS` in run.py. Also
change `small, medium, large = results` to `small, medium, large, *extra = results`, and add a fourth
2. Set `provider: anthropic` (or openai, gemini) in config.yaml, with the key in .env and `uv sync
--extra cloud`. Read only the classify column: latency and memory are Ollama's, and the script stops
3. In run.py, delete `format=LABEL_SCHEMA` from the classification chat call and change the `Reply as
JSON` line in `CLASSIFY` to 'Reply with one word: threat, logistics or personal.' What happens to
4. No edit: run make lesson N=12 twice. After each run, git diff docs/charts/12-model-scorecard.json
More detail: 'Try this' in lessons/12-choosing-a-model/README.md. Undo an edit with git checkout <file>,
or set every change aside with git stash.
On these sixteen messages the small model scores 69%, the medium 69% and the large 81%. The small model
cannot reliably copy an invoice number into the right field. The most accurate, qwen3:4b, costs 2.8x the
medium model's time per message and 3.9 GB of memory, on a machine that runs everything else in the
building. None of them sorts threats well enough to go unsupervised.
You write the policy down for Hale: the medium model for bulk triage, the large one for findings that go
to court, and a person reads every message marked as a threat. Model, version, settings, test and score
are in the file. Varma signs it. "Now make sure it still holds when they change the models."
